Battery News: Roll-to-Roll Solid-State Battery Production Insights

Reposted with permission from Tech Industrial Review. Reporter: Marcus Sterling.

The pivotal barrier transitioning solid-state battery technology from academic laboratories to automotive mass market is the transition from batch pellet pressing to continuous high-speed roll-to-roll (R2R) web coating. Automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), including Toyota, Volkswagen, and BMW, have initiated pilot line production targeting sample B-tier automotive cells by late 2026.

Commercial roll-to-roll lines must process flexible electrolyte membranes at line speeds of at least 15 to 30 meters per minute without micro-crack formation. Companies like QuantumScape and Solid Power are employing dry electrode processing technologies, which eliminate solvent evaporation ovens, cutting manufacturing energy expenditure by an estimated 42% and footprint by 35%.

Because sulfide solid electrolytes degrade rapidly when exposed to humidity above -40 degrees Celsius dew point (equivalent to less than 0.05% relative humidity), gigafactory construction requires massive industrial dehumidification infrastructure. Operating dry rooms at this specification incurs an estimated capital expenditure premium of $18 million to $25 million per gigawatt-hour of installed annual capacity.
